docs.title: Sentinel DV
docs.text:
Verification intelligence for AI agents

Read-only Model Context Protocol access to SystemVerilog, UVM, and cocotb artifacts—indexed with DuckDB, validated against versioned schemas, and bounded for safe LLM reasoning.

Get started MCP tool gallery View on GitHub

docs.title: Why Sentinel DV
docs.text:
• Security first

    Read-only MCP tools with path sandboxing, automatic redaction, and bounded outputs. No simulator control or artifact modification.

    Security model

  • Schema-driven

    Every response conforms to versioned, typed contracts. Deterministic outputs support reliable agent reasoning.

    Schema reference

  • Rich verification data

    Tests, failures, UVM topology, assertions, coverage, and regression analytics—across 26 MCP tools.

    Tool reference

  • Simulator agnostic

    VCS, Xcelium, Questa, Verilator, and more via adapter plugins and unified schemas.

    Simulator support

  • Indexed queries

    DuckDB-backed indexing with pagination and selective projection for fast, bounded reads.

    Performance guide

  • Extensible adapters

    Plugin architecture for custom parsers and new artifact formats.

    Custom adapters

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: config.yaml (or config.yml) controls what Sentinel DV indexes and the safety limits it enforces on tool responses.

docs.title: Configuration is required
docs.text:
The MCP server and indexer do not start without a config file. Sentinel DV will not silently point at the bundled demo/ tree if you omit configuration.

Provide config in one of these ways:

  1. --config /absolute/path/to/config.yaml on sentinel-dv-server and sentinel-dv-index
  2. SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG environment variable (same path)
  3. config.yaml or config.yml in the process current working directory

Copy the template from the repository root:

cp config.example.yaml config.yaml
# edit artifact_roots and index.path, then index and start the server

For trying examples only, use the demo-specific templates (e.g. cp demo/config.example.yaml demo/config.yaml).

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
artifact_roots:
  - /path/to/verification/regressions

index:
  type: duckdb
  path: ./sentinel_dv.db

adapters:
  uvm: true
  cocotb: true
  assertions: true
  coverage: true
  waveform_summary: false  # index *.wave.json and *.vcd (see guides/waveforms.md)

security:
  max_response_bytes: 2097152
  max_page_size: 200
  max_evidence_refs: 10
  max_excerpt_length: 1024
  max_message_length: 4096
  max_tags_per_event: 20
  max_coverage_metrics: 200
  max_bins_missed: 50

redaction:
  enabled: true
  patterns: []
  redact_emails: true
  redact_ips: false
  redact_paths: true

docs.title: Where to set the config path
docs.text:
You can either pass --config /path/to/config.yaml to the server/indexer, or set:

export SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/config.yaml

docs.title: Installation (5 minutes)
docs.text:
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/kiranreddi/sentinel-dv.git
cd sentinel-dv

# 2. Create virtual environment
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# 3. Install dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

# 4. Verify installation
python -m sentinel_dv.server --help

docs.title: First Index (10 minutes)
docs.text:
# 1. Create configuration
cp config.example.yaml config.yaml

# 2. Edit config.yaml to point to your artifacts
nano config.yaml
# Set artifact_roots to your verification directories

# 3. Index demo artifacts (test the system)
python -m sentinel_dv.indexing.indexer \
    --config config.yaml \
    --index-all

# 4. Check index was created
ls -lh sentinel_dv.db

docs.title: Start Server (2 minutes)
docs.text:
# Start the MCP server
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config config.yaml

# Server is now ready for MCP clients!

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. Indexing Phase (offline)
  2. Adapters parse raw artifacts
  3. Data is normalized and classified
  4. IDs are generated deterministically

  5. Everything stored in DuckDB

  6. Query Phase (runtime)

  7. MCP client sends tool request
  8. Server queries DuckDB index
  9. Results are paginated and returned
  10. All responses are typed and validated

docs.title: Custom MCP Client
docs.text:
from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

async def query_sentinel_dv():
    server_params = StdioServerParameters(
        command="python",
        args=["-m", "sentinel_dv.server", "--config", "config.yaml"]
    )

    async with stdio_client(server_params) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            # Initialize
            await session.initialize()

            # List failing tests
            result = await session.call_tool("tests.list", {
                "status": "fail",
                "page": 1,
                "page_size": 10
            })

            print(result)

docs.title: Workflow 5: Assertion and coverage intelligence
docs.text:
In Claude:

"List APB assertions and show failures in this run between 2us and 3us"
→ Uses: assertions.list with protocol/tag filters, then assertions.failures with start_time_ns/end_time_ns

"Show bounded functional coverage with evidence for latest run"
→ Uses: coverage.list, then coverage.summary with include_evidence=true

Tips: - assertions.list supports deterministic filtering by scope, name_pattern, protocol, and tag. - coverage.summary is bounded by security.max_coverage_metrics and security.max_bins_missed. - assertions.failures time windows require both start_time_ns and end_time_ns.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• Stability: IDs must remain stable across machines, paths, and indexing time
  • Determinism: Same artifacts + same config ⇒ identical IDs
  • Collision resistance: Use cryptographic hashing
  • Privacy: Avoid embedding sensitive raw strings; hash normalized representations instead
  • Traceability: IDs must be reproducible from stored index fields

docs.title: Hash Algorithm
docs.text:
• Primary: SHA-256
  • ID encoding: lowercase hex
  • ID format: <prefix>_<hex12> for compact IDs exposed via MCP; store full sha256 internally
  • Example: t_ab12cd34ef56

Rationale: Clients get short IDs; store retains full hash for collision detection and audit.

docs.title: Canonical Serialization
docs.text:
All hash inputs must use a canonical serialization:

  • JSON with:
  • sorted keys
  • UTF-8 encoding
  • no whitespace
  • Normalize strings (see below) before serialization

docs.title: String Normalization
docs.text:
Applies to all ID inputs:

  • Trim leading/trailing whitespace
  • Normalize line endings to \n
  • Lowercase where the semantic field is case-insensitive (e.g., framework name, simulator vendor)
  • Replace platform-dependent path separators (\ → /)
  • Remove volatile substrings (see "Volatile stripping")

docs.title: Volatile Stripping (for stability)
docs.text:
Remove/normalize values known to vary between runs but not semantically part of identity:

  • Absolute filesystem prefixes (replace with <ROOT> before hashing)
  • Hostnames (replace with <HOST>)
  • Timestamps (replace with <TS>)
  • Random temporary directory names (replace with <TMP>)

This is applied only where those values might leak into identity fields (typically evidence paths and raw messages).

docs.title: Preferred (CI-backed) run_id
docs.text:
If CI metadata exists:

run_id_full = sha256(canonical_json({
    "suite": <suite>,
    "ci_system": <ci.system>,
    "ci_build_id": <ci.build_id>,
    "ci_job_url": <normalized_url(ci.job_url)>
}))

docs.title: Fallback (artifact-backed) run_id
docs.text:
If CI metadata is absent:

# Use stable fingerprint of the artifact set
artifact_manifest_hash = sha256(concat(sorted([
    relative_path + ":" + file_sha256
])))

run_id_full = sha256(canonical_json({
    "suite": <suite>,
    "artifact_manifest": <artifact_manifest_hash>
}))

docs.title: Exposed run_id
docs.text: run_id = "r_" + hex12(run_id_full)

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
A test_id should uniquely identify a test instance within a run.

Hash input:

{
  "run_id_full": "<full sha256 of run_id>",
  "framework": "uvm|cocotb|sv_unit|unknown",
  "test_name": "<normalized test name>",
  "seed": <int|null>,
  "simulator_vendor": "<normalized vendor|null>",
  "simulator_version": "<normalized version|null>",
  "dut_top": "<normalized top|null>"
}

Notes: - seed is included when present because it materially changes behavior in DV - If your environment has an explicit test GUID (some harnesses do), include that as test_guid and optionally omit other fields

docs.title: Computation
docs.text:
test_id_full = sha256(canonical_json(inputs))
test_id = "t_" + hex12(test_id_full)

docs.title: What a Failure Event Is
docs.text:
A FailureEvent is a normalized record of something that went wrong, typically derived from:

  • UVM report lines
  • cocotb exception traces
  • assertion failure entries
  • compile/elab errors

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Failures must be uniquely addressable within a test, but stable across indexing.

Hash input:

{
  "test_id_full": "<full sha256 of test_id>",
  "severity": "info|warning|error|fatal",
  "category": "...",
  "summary_norm": "<normalized summary>",
  "component_norm": "<normalized component|null>",
  "phase_norm": "<normalized phase|null>",
  "time_bucket": "<time bucket|null>",
  "evidence_fingerprint": "<optional>"
}

docs.title: time_bucket
docs.text:
To prevent instability from minor timestamp differences, use bucketing:

  • If time is available: time_bucket = floor(time_ns / 1000) (1 µs buckets)
  • If only log line exists without time: null

docs.title: evidence_fingerprint
docs.text:
Optional but useful when multiple identical summaries exist:

evidence_fingerprint = sha256(concat(sorted([
    path + ":" + start_line + ":" + end_line
])))

Only include if evidence exists; otherwise omit.

docs.title: Computation
docs.text:
failure_id_full = sha256(canonical_json(inputs))
failure_id = "f_" + hex12(failure_id_full)

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A FailureSignature clusters failures across tests/runs.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Signature should represent the type of failure, not the instance.

Hash input:

{
  "category": "...",
  "summary_signature": "<signature-normalized summary>",
  "protocol": "<protocol tag|null>",
  "component_role": "<optional normalized role|null>"
}

docs.title: signature-normalized summary
docs.text:
Apply stronger normalization than summary_norm:

  • Replace hex literals: 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+ → <HEX>
  • Replace decimal numbers: \b\d+\b → <NUM>
  • Replace time units: 123ns, 45 us → <TIME>
  • Replace paths: /.../file.sv → <PATH>
  • Replace instance paths: tb.top.env.agent[3].drv → <INST> (optional, configurable)
  • Collapse whitespace

docs.title: Computation
docs.text:
signature_id_full = sha256(canonical_json(inputs))
signature_id = "s_" + hex12(signature_id_full)

docs.title: Collision Handling
docs.text:
• Store full hashes (*_id_full) in the index
  • If two different records yield same short ID (hex12 collision), server must:
  • still disambiguate internally by full hash
  • expose a longer prefix (configurable) for those IDs or include full hash in details responses
  • In practice, SHA-256 with 12 hex chars (48 bits) is typically sufficient, but collision handling must exist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Sentinel DV uses an index store to serve MCP tools efficiently and deterministically from potentially massive artifact trees.

docs.title: Storage Backend Recommendation (v1)
docs.text:
DuckDB is the recommended default:

  • Simple to ship and operate
  • Strong filtering and pagination
  • Deterministic queries
  • Excellent for analytical workloads (100k–100M rows)
  • Built-in support for complex aggregations

v1.x supports DuckDB only.

docs.title: Table: runs
docs.text:
Columns:

CREATE TABLE runs (
    run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,              -- short form, e.g., r_...
    run_id_full TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,     -- full sha256 hex
    suite TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,             -- RFC3339
    status TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- pass|fail|mixed|unknown
    ci_system TEXT,
    ci_build_id TEXT,
    ci_job_url TEXT,
    artifact_manifest_hash TEXT,
    index_built_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

Indexes:

CREATE INDEX idx_runs_suite_created_at ON runs(suite, created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_runs_ci_build ON runs(ci_system, ci_build_id);

docs.text:
Columns:

CREATE TABLE tests (
    test_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,             -- t_...
    test_id_full TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- REFERENCES runs(run_id)
    framework TEXT NOT NULL,
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    seed INTEGER,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- pass|fail|error|skipped|unknown
    duration_ms INTEGER,
    sim_vendor TEXT,
    sim_version TEXT,
    dut_top TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL              -- copied from run for easier filtering

Indexes:

CREATE INDEX idx_tests_run_status ON tests(run_id, status);
CREATE INDEX idx_tests_name ON tests(name);

docs.title: Query Semantics (How Tools Map to SQL)
Common Constraints
docs.text:
• Always apply page/page_size as: 
    LIMIT page_size OFFSET (page-1)*page_size
  • Always return total_items computed via a separate COUNT(*) query with the same filters
  • Sorting must be stable: if sort field ties, add secondary sort on primary key (test_id, failure_id) to keep deterministic ordering

docs.title: tests.list
docs.text:
Filters map to WHERE clauses:

  • run_id = ?
  • framework = ?
  • status = ?
  • name LIKE %?% (escape wildcards)
  • seed = ?

docs.title: failures.list
docs.text:
Filters map to WHERE clauses:

  • test_id = ? or run_id = ?
  • category = ?
  • severity = ?
  • component LIKE %?%
  • Tags:
  • For v1, tags stored as JSON string; simplest deterministic approach:
    • precompute a tags_flat TEXT column (space-delimited normalized tags) and query with LIKE
    • or use DuckDB's JSON functions: json_extract

Recommended: Store both: - tags_json - tags_flat (lowercase, space delimited, bounded)

Then tags_any → OR of tags_flat LIKE %tag%.

docs.title: regressions.summary
docs.text:
Compute:

  • pass rate: count tests by status across runs in window
  • top signatures: group failures by signature_id and count distinct tests (or failures)

Recommended: define clearly: - count = number of occurrences (failures) - optionally affected_tests = count distinct test_id

Use deterministic top-N ordering: - order by affected_tests desc, then count desc, then signature_id asc

docs.title: runs.diff
docs.text:
Deterministic diff components:

  1. Test status changes:

  2. join tests by (framework, name, seed) (or by stable test GUID if available)

  3. Signature changes:

  4. signatures in compare not in base → "new"

  5. in base not in compare → "resolved"

  6. Coverage deltas:

  7. compare coverage metrics by (kind, name, scope) for shared keys

  8. Config deltas:

  9. only if config snapshot is indexed (optional v1.1)

docs.title: Indexing Phases
docs.text:
1. Discover runs and their artifact roots
  2. Parse adapters producing normalized records
  3. Compute IDs and signatures
  4. Apply redaction and bounding
  5. Write to DuckDB in a transaction
  6. Record index_built_at and schema version

docs.title: Incremental Indexing (optional)
docs.text:
• Use artifact_manifest_hash changes to detect whether a run needs reindex
  • For CI-backed runs, prefer ci_build_id + suite as key

docs.title: Integrity and Reproducibility Fields (recommended)
docs.text: Include in index metadata table:

docs.title: Table: meta
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE meta (
    key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    value TEXT NOT NULL
);

Suggested keys:

  • schema_version
  • indexer_version
  • built_at
  • config_hash (sha256 of normalized config affecting indexing)

This supports "same inputs → same outputs" audits.

docs.title: Tight Coupling Decisions (explicit)
docs.text:
• IDs depend only on normalized semantic fields, not on indexing time
  • Signature IDs depend only on category + signature-normalized summary (+ optional tags)
  • Taxonomy rules are ordered and versioned; changes should increment MINOR or MAJOR depending on whether it changes enum behavior significantly

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Normalize noisy verification outputs into consistent:
  • severity
  • category
  • tags[]
  • Provide deterministic, explainable mapping from source text → taxonomy

docs.title: Taxonomy Categories (v1)
docs.text:
FailureEvent.category enum:

  • assertion
  • scoreboard
  • protocol
  • timeout
  • xprop
  • compile
  • elab
  • runtime
  • unknown

docs.title: UVM Severity Normalization
docs.text:
Map to:

  • UVM_INFO → info
  • UVM_WARNING → warning
  • UVM_ERROR → error
  • UVM_FATAL → fatal

If a simulator prefixes errors differently (e.g., *E, in Xcelium), map to error unless fatal keywords exist.

docs.title: cocotb Severity Normalization
docs.text:
• Exception in test → error
  • Explicit assertion failure → fail at test level, but failure events often still error unless you distinguish "check failure" vs "infrastructure error"

Recommended: - If message matches AssertionError, ScoreboardMismatch, or user "expect" failure → error but category scoreboard/protocol/assertion as appropriate - If matches ImportError, RuntimeError at harness, SimulatorError → runtime + severity fatal (configurable)

docs.title: Category Mapping Rules (ordered, first match wins)
Rule Group A: Compile / Elaboration (highest priority)
1. Compile
docs.text:
Patterns: - Compilation failed - Error-[A-Z0-9]+ with compile - vlog- / xmvlog errors - Syntax error, unexpected token, Undefined variable in compile context

Category: compile Tags: ["compile"] + vendor tags

docs.title: 2. Elaboration
docs.text:
Patterns: - Elaboration failed - Unresolved reference (during elab) - Cannot find instance / binding failed - Top module not found

Category: elab Tags: ["elab"]

docs.title: 3. Assertion Failures
docs.text:
Patterns: - ASSERTION FAILED - SVA and failed - assert property failure messages - Vendor-specific: - Questa: ** Error: (vsim-*) with assertion wording - VCS: Assertion failure / $assertoff contexts

Category: assertion Tags: ["assertion", "sva"] + protocol tags if detectable (AXI/APB/etc.)

If an assertion name is captured, attach it to: - AssertionFailure.assertion_id (when resolvable) - FailureEvent.tags += ["assert:<name>"] (bounded)

docs.title: 4. Timeout
docs.text:
Patterns: - TIMEOUT - watchdog - No activity for - objection timeout - phase timeout - simulation time limit reached

Category: timeout Tags: ["timeout"] + phase tags if known (e.g., phase:run)

docs.title: 5. Xprop / X-Check
docs.text:
Patterns: - X-propagation - X-check - Unknown value X - has Xs - xrun: *E combined with X warnings (vendor-specific)

Category: xprop Tags: ["xprop"]

docs.title: Rule Group E: Scoreboard / Data Mismatches
6. Scoreboard Mismatch
docs.text:
Patterns: - scoreboard and (mismatch|compare failed|unexpected|expected) - DATA MISMATCH - CRC mismatch (often protocol too; see tags) - sequence item mismatch

Category: scoreboard Tags: ["scoreboard"] + protocol tags if detectable

docs.title: Rule Group F: Protocol Violations (when explicit)
7. Protocol
docs.text:
Patterns: - protocol violation - handshake violation - illegal transition - unexpected response (when not scoreboard compare) - BRESP/RRESP error codes in AXI monitors - APB PSLVERR in monitor

Category: protocol Tags: ["protocol"] + protocol name tags

docs.title: 8. Runtime
docs.text:
Patterns: - segmentation fault - core dumped - Simulator terminated - Python traceback that indicates harness failure - Out of memory - License checkout failed

Category: runtime Severity: fatal for crashes/license failures; otherwise error Tags: ["runtime"]

docs.title: 9. Unknown
docs.text: Category: unknown Tags: derived from heuristic keyword extraction (bounded)

docs.title: Standard Tags (recommended)
docs.text:
• Vendor: vcs, questa, xcelium, verilator, riviera
  • Framework: uvm, cocotb
  • Protocol: axi4, ahb, apb, pcie, usb, jtag, i2c, spi, gpio
  • Phase: phase:build, phase:connect, phase:run, phase:shutdown
  • Component role: driver, monitor, scoreboard, sequencer

docs.title: Protocol Detection Heuristics
docs.text:
If message contains:

  • AXI or AWVALID/WREADY/BRESP → tag axi4
  • PADDR/PSEL/PREADY/PSLVERR → tag apb
  • HADDR/HREADY/HRESP → tag ahb
  • LTSSM, TS1, TS2 → tag pcie
  • LFPS, PIPE, U0/U1/U2 → tag usb
  • TMS, TCK, TDO, TDI → tag jtag

docs.title: Bounded Tagging
docs.text:
• Max tags per failure: 20
  • Prefer deterministic ordering: [category/framework/protocol/vendor/phase/component_role/other]

docs.title: Evidence Linkage Policy
docs.text:
When a taxonomy decision is made, the indexer may store:

  • taxonomy_reason: a short code like RULE_ASSERTION_VENDOR_QUES (optional internal field)
  • This reason is not required to be exposed via MCP in v1, but helps debugging

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Coverage HTML parsing — VCS URG (dashboard.html): Sentinel DV now automatically detects and parses VCS URG dashboard.html reports generated by urg -report. Extracted metrics: SCORE, LINE, TOGGLE, ASSERT, GROUP, and Verification Plan score. No configuration required — add the coverage report directory to artifact_roots.
  • Coverage HTML parsing — Questa vcover (overalldu.js): Sentinel DV now automatically detects and parses Questa vcover files/overalldu.js data files (generated by vcover report -html). Extracted metrics: statement, branch, toggle, assertion, functional (covergroup), and total coverage percentages with exact hit/total counts. Add the HTML report's files/ subdirectory to artifact_roots.
  • Both parsers are guarded by content-sniffing so that only genuine VCS URG / Questa HTML report files are matched (not any arbitrary dashboard.html or overalldu.js).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• UVM parser: false-positive failures from count-summary lines — VCS logs end with UVM_ERROR : 0 / UVM_FATAL : 0 and Questa logs with # UVM_ERROR : 0. These were matched by the generic fallback pattern and stored as real failures. A new UVM_COUNT_SUMMARY_PATTERN now skips them before any other pattern is attempted. Impact on 1197-run real CI dataset: 16 240 → 4 380 indexed failures (11 860 false positives eliminated).
  • UVM parser: passing tests marked fail — TEST_FAILED_PATTERN contained \bUVM_FATAL\b which matched the count-summary line UVM_FATAL : 0 in otherwise-passing logs, producing spurious status=fail on passing tests. Removed \bUVM_FATAL\b from the pattern; fatal detection is done via the parsed messages list where count-summary lines are already excluded.
  • MCP output schema validation (_ITEM_ENVELOPE) — FastMCP validates tool output against the declared JSON schema. Error responses return {schema_version, error: {...}} with no item key, which failed schema validation for get/topology tools. Fixed by making item optional (only schema_version is required).
  • Coverage text parser regex (_LINE_PATTERN) — ambiguous optional-scope group could match a prefix of the coverage kind (e.g. scope="Branc" kind="h" instead of scope=None kind="Branch"). Fixed by requiring a colon delimiter after scope: (?:(?P<scope>…)\s*:\s*)?(?P<kind>\w+)\s+coverage:.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• DV Intelligence Tool 1 — Coverage Trend (coverage.trend): time-series coverage trajectory across runs. Computes per-run coverage percentages with deltas and characterizes trend direction as improving, stalling, or declining.
  • DV Intelligence Tool 2 — Cross-Simulator Divergence (runs.cross_sim): detects tests that pass on one simulator vendor but fail on another. Surfaces critical divergences that must be resolved before sign-off.
  • DV Intelligence Tool 3 — Failure Clustering (tests.cluster): groups failures by root-cause signature using message and category similarity, reducing hundreds of failures to a handful of actionable clusters for faster triage.
  • DV Intelligence Tool 4 — Regression Health Score (regression.health): composite 0–100 DV readiness score with weighted sub-scores for pass rate (30%), coverage (35%), assertion health (15%), flakiness (10%), and cross-simulator consistency (10%). Outputs band: sign-off-ready | minor-issues | coverage-gaps | not-ready.
  • DV Intelligence Tool 5 — Coverage Advisor (coverage.advisor): generates ready-to-paste SystemVerilog constraint and UVM sequence snippets for uncovered bins. Protocol-aware for AXI4, AHB, APB, CHI, PCIe naming patterns.
  • sentinel_dv/normalization/coverage_advisor.py: new module — _PROTOCOL_RULES knowledge base + build_advisories() entry point.
  • New store methods: coverage_trend(), cross_sim_divergence(), cluster_failures(), regression_health_data().

If you discover a security vulnerability in Sentinel DV, please report it responsibly:

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: Sentinel DV is designed with security as a core principle. See Architecture → Security for the complete security model.

docs.title: Key Security Features
docs.text:
1. Read-Only Design - MCP tools only read verification data - No write, delete, or modify operations - Prevents accidental or malicious data corruption

2. Automatic Redaction - Credentials automatically removed from logs - File paths sanitized - Sensitive data filtered before exposure

3. Path Sandboxing - File access restricted to allowed paths - Path traversal attacks prevented - Symbolic link following disabled

4. Bounded Outputs - Response size limits prevent DoS - Pagination enforced for large datasets - Memory usage capped

5. Input Validation - All inputs validated with Pydantic schemas - SQL injection prevented (parameterized queries) - No arbitrary code execution

Security patches are backported to the latest stable release only.

docs.title: For Users
docs.text:
1. Configure Path Restrictions 

# Restrict file access by configuring `artifact_roots` in `config.yaml`.
# The server validates that roots exist and are readable at startup.
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config config.yaml

2. Use Separate Databases 

# Use separate `config.yaml` files with different `index.path` values.
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config ./config-prod.yaml  # Production
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config ./config-dev.yaml   # Development

3. Regular Updates 

# Keep Sentinel DV up to date
pip install --upgrade sentinel-dv

4. Monitor Logs 

# Run under your process manager and collect stdout/stderr logs.
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config config.yaml

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
1. Validate All Inputs 

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class SafeInput(BaseModel):
    run_id: str = Field(pattern=r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$")
    page: int = Field(ge=1, le=1000)

2. Sanitize Outputs 

def redact_credentials(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove credentials from text."""
    patterns = [
        r"(password|token|key|secret)[:=]\s*[^\s]+",
        r"Bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9_-]+",
    ]
    for pattern in patterns:
        text = re.sub(pattern, r"\1: [REDACTED]", text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    return text

3. Limit Resource Usage 

MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100
MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE = 10 * 1024 * 1024  # 10MB

def safe_query(page_size: int):
    if page_size > MAX_PAGE_SIZE:
        raise ValueError(f"Page size exceeds maximum ({MAX_PAGE_SIZE})")
    # Execute query...

4. Use Parameterized Queries 

# ✅ Good - parameterized
cursor.execute(
    "SELECT * FROM tests WHERE run_id = ?",
    (run_id,)
)

# ❌ Bad - SQL injection risk
cursor.execute(
    f"SELECT * FROM tests WHERE run_id = '{run_id}'"
)

docs.title: 1. Local File Access
docs.text:
Risk: Sentinel DV indexes local files Mitigation: - Configure path access by setting artifact_roots in config.yaml. - Run with least-privilege user account - Use read-only file mounts in Docker

Example: 

# Docker with read-only mount
docker run -v ./verification:/data:ro sentinel-dv:latest

docs.title: 2. Database Access
docs.text:
Risk: Index database contains indexed data Mitigation: - Restrict database file permissions (chmod 600) - Store in secure directory - Encrypt at rest if needed

Example: 

# Secure database permissions
chmod 600 ./sentinel_db/index.db
chown sentinel-user:sentinel-group ./sentinel_db/index.db

docs.title: 3. MCP Communication
docs.text: Risk: MCP protocol uses stdio communication Mitigation: - MCP servers run locally only (no network exposure) - Communication authenticated by AI client (Claude/Cline) - No external network access required

docs.title: 4. Log Parsing
docs.text:
Risk: Parsing untrusted log files Mitigation: - No code execution from logs - Regex patterns bounded - File size limits enforced - Timeout for parsing operations

Example: 

MAX_FILE_SIZE = 100 * 1024 * 1024  # 100MB
PARSE_TIMEOUT = 30  # seconds

@timeout(PARSE_TIMEOUT)
def parse_log(file_path: str):
    if os.path.getsize(file_path) > MAX_FILE_SIZE:
        raise ValueError("File too large")
    # Parse...

docs.title: Custom Adapters
docs.text:
Sentinel DV currently ships a fixed built-in adapter set:

  • sentinel_dv.adapters.uvm_log.UVMLogParser
  • sentinel_dv.adapters.cocotb.CocotbParser
  • sentinel_dv.adapters.assertion_reports.AssertionReportParser
  • sentinel_dv.adapters.coverage_reports.CoverageReportParser
  • sentinel_dv.adapters.waveform_summary.WaveformSummaryParser
  • sentinel_dv.adapters.vcd_summary.VcdSummaryParser

docs.title: Important: What is and is not supported today
docs.text:
• There is no runtime plugin registry API today.
  • There is no SentinelDV.register_adapter(...) public API.
  • There is no config-driven dynamic adapter loading (module/class/priority) yet.

This page describes the current internal adapter contract and the safest extension path for contributors.

docs.title: Current internal adapter contract
docs.text:
Built-in adapters generally follow:

  • can_handle(path: Path) -> bool
  • parse(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]

The indexer calls these directly and normalizes output into store tables.

docs.title: Recommended extension path (current architecture)
docs.text:
If you need a new format:

  1. Add a parser under sentinel_dv/adapters/ with can_handle + parse.
  2. Add focused tests under tests/unit/ for malformed and happy-path inputs.
  3. Wire discovery + ingestion in sentinel_dv/indexing/indexer.py.
  4. Keep outputs bounded and deterministic:
  5. relative paths only
  6. redacted excerpts
  7. deterministic sorting and IDs

docs.title: Future plugin model
docs.text: A first-class adapter plugin registry is planned but not implemented in v1.2.x. Until then, adapter additions are code changes in-repo.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: Sentinel DV is designed with security-first principles and strict separation of concerns.

docs.title: 1. Read-Only by Design
docs.text:
No mutations, no control:

  • All tools are strictly read-only
  • No simulator triggers or job submissions
  • No artifact modification
  • No configuration changes via API

Enforcement:

# All file operations use read-only modes
with open(artifact_path, 'r') as f:  # Never 'w' or 'a'
    data = f.read()

docs.title: 2. Schema-First Contracts
docs.text:
Every response conforms to versioned schemas:

from sentinel_dv.schemas import TestCase

# Response structure is deterministic
test: TestCase = {
    "id": "T123",
    "framework": "uvm",
    "status": "fail",
    ...
}

Benefits:

  • LLMs can reason reliably
  • Backward compatibility guarantees
  • Self-documenting APIs
  • Testable contracts

docs.title: 3. Deterministic Outputs
docs.text:
Same input → same output:

  • No LLM-generated fields in responses
  • All facts derived from artifacts
  • Stable signature hashing
  • Reproducible indexing

docs.title: 4. Evidence-Based Facts
docs.text:
Every fact traceable to source:

failure: FailureEvent = {
    "message": "AXI BRESP error",
    "evidence": [
        {
            "kind": "log",
            "path": "test.log",
            "span": {"start_line": 142, "end_line": 148},
            "extract": "...",
            "hash": "sha256..."
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: 5. Security Boundaries
docs.text:
Defense in depth:

  1. Path sandboxing - Only configured roots accessible
  2. Automatic redaction - Secrets/PII removed
  3. Size limits - Prevent DoS and prompt injection
  4. Input validation - Pydantic schemas
  5. Fail-safe defaults - Conservative limits

docs.title: Indexing Flow
docs.text:
Artifact Roots → Adapters → Normalization → Index Store
                    ↓           ↓              ↓
                Raw Parse   Redact &      DuckDB
                            Categorize

Steps:

  1. Scan configured artifact roots
  2. Parse files using enabled adapters
  3. Normalize extracted data (redaction, signatures)
  4. Store in indexed database
  5. Build lookup indexes for fast queries

docs.title: Query Flow
docs.text:
MCP Request → Tool → Query Builder → Index Store → Normalization → Response
                ↓          ↓              ↓             ↓              ↓
           Validate   SQL/Filter     DuckDB       Redact        Schema
           Input      Construction    Query        Evidence      Serialize

Steps:

  1. Receive MCP tool call
  2. Validate input parameters
  3. Build database query with filters/pagination
  4. Execute query against index
  5. Normalize results (redaction, bounding)
  6. Serialize to schema-compliant JSON

docs.title: DuckDB Schema
docs.text:
-- Runs table
CREATE TABLE runs (
    run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    suite TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMP,
    ci_system TEXT,
    ci_job_url TEXT,
    ci_build_id TEXT
);

-- Tests table
CREATE TABLE tests (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id TEXT,
    framework TEXT,
    name TEXT,
    status TEXT,
    duration_ms INTEGER,
    seed INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES runs(run_id)

-- Failures table
CREATE TABLE failures (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    test_id TEXT,
    category TEXT,
    severity TEXT,
    summary TEXT,
    message TEXT,
    time_ns INTEGER,
    signature_id TEXT,
    FOREIGN KEY (test_id) REFERENCES tests(id)

docs.title: Schema Reference
docs.text: All Sentinel DV responses conform to versioned, typed schemas for reliable LLM reasoning.

docs.title: Schema Versioning
docs.text:
Every response includes a schema_version field:

{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "data": {...}
}

Version Format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (semver) - MAJOR: Breaking changes (field removals, type changes) - MINOR: Additive changes (new fields, new enum values) - PATCH: Bug fixes (no schema impact)

docs.title: RunRef
docs.text:
Reference to a verification run.

class RunRef(BaseModel):
    run_id: str
    run_id_full: str | None = None
    suite: str | None = None
    created_at: str | None = None  # RFC3339 timestamp

Example: 

{
  "run_id": "R20260125_143000",
  "run_id_full": "R20260125_143000_NIGHTLY_GH12345",
  "suite": "nightly",
  "created_at": "2026-01-25T14:30:00Z"
}

docs.title: TestCase
docs.text:
Complete test result information.

class TestCase(BaseModel):
    id: str  # T20260125_143000_test_name
    framework: Framework  # "uvm" | "cocotb" | "sv_unit" | "unknown"
    name: str
    seed: int | None = None
    simulator: SimulatorInfo | None = None
    dut: DutInfo | None = None
    status: TestStatus  # "pass" | "fail" | "error" | "skipped" | "unknown"
    duration_ms: int | None = None
    run: RunRef
    evidence: list[EvidenceRef] = []

Example: 

{
  "id": "T20260125_143000_axi_burst_test",
  "framework": "uvm",
  "name": "axi_burst_test",
  "seed": 42,
  "simulator": {
    "vendor": "VCS",
    "version": "2023.12"
  },
  "dut": {
    "top": "axi_interconnect",
    "config": {"NUM_MASTERS": "4", "DATA_WIDTH": "64"}
  },
  "status": "fail",
  "duration_ms": 15420,
  "run": {
    "run_id": "R20260125_143000",
    "suite": "nightly"
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "kind": "log",
      "path": "axi_burst_test.log",
      "span": {"start_line": 1, "end_line": 450}
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: FailureEvent
docs.text:
Categorized failure information.

class FailureEvent(BaseModel):
    id: str | None = None  # F20260125_143000_001
    test_id: str | None = None
    severity: Severity  # "info" | "warning" | "error" | "fatal"
    category: Category  # "assertion" | "scoreboard" | "protocol" | ...
    summary: str
    message: str
    time_ns: int | None = None
    phase: str | None = None
    component: str | None = None
    tags: list[str] = []
    evidence: list[EvidenceRef] = []

Categories: - assertion: Assertion failures (SVA, PSL, etc.) - scoreboard: Data mismatch in checkers - protocol: Protocol violations (AXI, PCIe, etc.) - timeout: Timeout errors - syntax: Compilation/syntax errors - configuration: Configuration issues - resource: Resource exhaustion - unknown: Uncategorized

Example: 

{
  "id": "F20260125_143000_001",
  "test_id": "T20260125_143000_axi_burst_test",
  "severity": "error",
  "category": "scoreboard",
  "summary": "DATA MISMATCH: Expected 0xDEAD, Got 0xBEEF",
  "message": "Scoreboard check failed at address 0x1000...",
  "time_ns": 100000,
  "phase": "main_phase",
  "component": "uvm_test_top.env.scoreboard",
  "tags": ["scoreboard", "data-integrity", "write-path"],
  "evidence": [
    {
      "kind": "log",
      "path": "axi_burst_test.log",
      "span": {"start_line": 234, "end_line": 234},
      "extract": "UVM_ERROR @ 100 ns: DATA MISMATCH..."
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text: Sentinel DV implements defense-in-depth security for AI agent access to verification artifacts.

docs.title: 1. Read-Only by Design
docs.text:
No Simulator Control - Cannot run simulations - Cannot execute commands - Cannot modify artifacts - Cannot access system resources

Query-Only Interface - All tools are read-only queries - No write operations exposed - No configuration changes via MCP - Immutable indexed data

docs.title: 2. Automatic Redaction
docs.text:
All outputs are automatically scanned and sensitive data is redacted:

Credentials 

AWS Keys:     AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE → [REDACTED]
GitHub PATs:  ghp_abc123... → [REDACTED]
OpenAI Keys:  sk-proj-abc... → [REDACTED]
GitLab Tokens: glpat-xxx... → [REDACTED]
Bearer Tokens: Bearer abc... → [REDACTED]
SSH Keys:     ssh-rsa AAA... → [REDACTED]

File Paths 

Absolute:  /home/user/project/sim.log → [REDACTED]
Home dir:  ~/workspace/test.log → [REDACTED]
Relative:  results/test.log → results/test.log ✓

Configurable Redaction 

# config.yaml
security:
  redaction:
    redact_emails: false  # Optional: redact email addresses
    redact_paths: true    # Recommended: redact absolute paths
    custom_patterns:
      - pattern: "INTERNAL_TOKEN_\\w+"
        replacement: "[INTERNAL_TOKEN]"

docs.title: 3. Path Sandboxing
docs.text:
All file path references are validated and constrained:

Allowed Paths - ✅ Relative paths within artifact_roots - ✅ Filenames without directory traversal - ✅ Paths validated against allow-list

Blocked Paths - ❌ Absolute paths (e.g., /etc/passwd) - ❌ Parent directory traversal (e.g., ../../secret) - ❌ Home directory references (e.g., ~/.ssh/) - ❌ Symlinks outside sandbox - ❌ Device files (e.g., /dev/null)

Implementation 

from sentinel_dv.schemas.common import EvidenceRef

# Valid - relative path
ref = EvidenceRef(kind="log", path="sim_results/test.log")

# Invalid - absolute path
ref = EvidenceRef(kind="log", path="/tmp/test.log")
# Raises: ValidationError: Absolute paths not allowed

# Invalid - traversal
ref = EvidenceRef(kind="log", path="../../../etc/passwd")
# Raises: ValidationError: Path traversal not allowed

docs.title: 4. Bounded Outputs
docs.text:
All responses have strict size limits to prevent denial-of-service:

Output Type Limit Rationale Log lines 1,000 lines Prevents memory exhaustion Text fields 50 KB Keeps LLM context manageable Array items 1,000 items Prevents infinite loops Page size 100 items Reasonable batch size Evidence extract 5,000 chars Sufficient for context

Automatic Truncation 

# Long text is automatically truncated
message = "..." * 100000
truncated = truncate_text(message, max_length=2000)
# Returns: first 2000 chars + "... (truncated)"

Pagination 

{
  "page": 1,
  "page_size": 50,  // Max 100
  "total_items": 1500,
  "items": [...]
}

docs.title: 5. Input Validation
docs.text:
All inputs are strictly validated using Pydantic schemas:

Type Safety 

# All inputs typed and validated
class TestsListInput(BaseModel):
    run_id: str = Field(..., min_length=1)
    framework: Framework | None = None  # Literal type
    status: TestStatus | None = None
    page: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)
    page_size: int = Field(default=50, ge=1, le=100)

Enum Constraints 

Framework = Literal["uvm", "cocotb", "sv_unit", "unknown"]
TestStatus = Literal["pass", "fail", "error", "skipped", "unknown"]
Severity = Literal["info", "warning", "error", "fatal"]

Pattern Validation 

# IDs must match specific patterns
run_id: str = Field(..., pattern=r"^R\d{8}_\d{6}$")
test_id: str = Field(..., pattern=r"^T\d{8}_\d{6}_\w+$")

docs.title: In Scope
docs.text:
1. Credential Leakage
  2. Mitigation: Automatic redaction
  3. Coverage: Common credential formats

  4. Configurable patterns

  5. Path Traversal

  6. Mitigation: Path sandboxing + validation
  7. Block: Absolute paths, .., symlinks

  8. Allow-list enforcement

  9. Resource Exhaustion (DoS)

  10. Mitigation: Bounded outputs + pagination
  11. Limits: File sizes, array lengths, text fields

  12. Timeouts: Query execution limits

  13. Data Injection

  14. Mitigation: Input validation + type safety
  15. No SQL injection (parameterized queries)
  16. No command injection (no shell execution)

docs.title: Out of Scope
docs.text:
1. Physical Access
  2. Requires: File system access control

  3. Defense: OS-level permissions

  4. Network Security

  5. Requires: HTTPS/TLS for transport

  6. Defense: MCP transport layer

  7. Authentication

  8. Handled by: MCP client (Claude Desktop)

  9. Not part of: Sentinel DV server

  10. Rate Limiting

  11. Handled by: MCP client
  12. Server-side: Query timeouts only

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Can Sentinel DV run simulations? A: No. It's read-only and only accesses pre-generated artifacts.

Q: Can I disable redaction? A: You can configure patterns, but path sandboxing is always enforced.

Q: What if I need absolute paths in evidence? A: Use relative paths from artifact_roots. They're more portable anyway.

Q: How do I add custom redaction patterns? A: Add them to security.redaction.custom_patterns in config.yaml.

Q: Is Sentinel DV safe for production verification data? A: Yes, with proper configuration. Enable all redactions and use restrictive artifact_roots.

docs.title: Production Deployment
docs.text:
Sentinel DV is an MCP server that runs locally over stdio (MCP clients such as Claude Desktop or Cursor). It is not a web HTTP service and is not deployed to Vercel or similar serverless hosts.

For “always on” deployments, you can run it under systemd.

docs.title: Server unit (example)
docs.text:
Create /etc/systemd/system/sentinel-dv.service:

[Unit]
Description=Sentinel DV MCP server
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=/path/to/sentinel-dv
Environment=PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
Environment=SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG=/path/to/config.yaml

ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 -m sentinel_dv.server

Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: Indexing
docs.text:
Indexing is a separate step. Run it at startup, before the server starts, or periodically with a systemd timer/cron.

Example one-shot indexing:

python -m sentinel_dv.indexing.indexer --config /path/to/config.yaml --index-all

sentinel-dv-index --config config.yaml --index-all
sentinel-dv-server --config config.yaml

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Current release: v2.1.0 (changelog)

This guide shows how to configure and run Sentinel DV locally, then connect it to an MCP client (e.g. Claude Desktop).

docs.title: From MCP Registry (recommended)
docs.text:
Use server name io.github.kiranreddi/sentinel-dv in an MCP registry–aware client, or run with uvx:

uvx --from sentinel-dv sentinel-dv-server --config /absolute/path/to/config.yaml

docs.title: From PyPI
docs.text:
pip install "sentinel-dv>=2.1.0"

Note: Do not install PyPI 1.0.0 (broken wheel). Use sentinel-dv>=2.1.0 for VCS/Questa/Cadence fixtures, assertion/coverage intelligence, VCD/JSON waveforms, and all 26 MCP tools. Verified flow: install → sentinel-dv-index --index-all → sentinel-dv-server → MCP tools.

For development:

pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: 2. Create config.yaml (required)
docs.text:
Sentinel DV requires a config file before indexing or serving MCP tools. There is no automatic demo/ fallback.

Copy the provided template and update:

cp config.example.yaml config.yaml

You may also use config.yml in the working directory, or set SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG / pass --config with any path you choose.

Edit config.yaml to set:

  • artifact_roots: directories that contain your verification artifacts (UVM *.log, cocotb JUnit XML like results.xml / junit.xml)
  • index.path: where the DuckDB database should be written
  • adapters: enable/disable parsers (booleans under uvm, cocotb, assertions, coverage, waveform_summary)
  • For waveforms: set waveform_summary: true and add *.wave.json and/or *.vcd files whose test_name matches indexed tests (see Waveform summaries and demo/verilator_counter/)

docs.title: 3. Index artifacts (required)
docs.text:
python -m sentinel_dv.indexing.indexer --config config.yaml --index-all

This scans the configured artifact_roots and rebuilds the index.

docs.title: 4. Start the MCP server (stdio)
docs.text:
python -m sentinel_dv.server --config config.yaml

Alternative: set the config path once:

export SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/config.yaml
python -m sentinel_dv.server

docs.title: 5. Connect via Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Add Sentinel DV to your Claude Desktop MCP config:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sentinel-dv": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": [
        "-m",
        "sentinel_dv.server",
        "--config",
        "/absolute/path/to/config.yaml"
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 6. Connect via Cline (VS Code)

      "command": "python",

        "-m",
        "sentinel_dv.server",

        "${workspaceFolder}/config.yaml"
      ]
    }
  }
}

  • If the server reports INDEX_NOT_READY, run the indexing step again.

docs.text:

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text: Sentinel DV indexes verification artifacts into DuckDB using a single, supported mode: full indexing via --index-all.

docs.title: Indexing performance (what you can tune)
docs.text:
1. Narrow your artifact_roots
  2. Point artifact_roots only at the directories you actually want indexed.

  3. This directly reduces the number of *.log, results.xml, and junit.xml files scanned.

  4. Use recognized artifact formats

  5. UVM logs: *.log
  6. cocotb results: results.xml / junit.xml

docs.title: Query performance (what you can tune)
docs.text:
1. Pagination

  2. List tools accept page and page_size and are clamped to security.max_page_size.

  3. Response sizing

  4. security.max_response_bytes limits how much data can be returned per tool call.

docs.title: Practical workflow
docs.text:
1. Start with a small subset of artifacts (few runs / a single directory).
  2. Run: python -m sentinel_dv.indexing.indexer --config config.yaml --index-all
  3. Validate your queries using list tools (runs.list, tests.list, failures.list, etc.).
  4. Increase scope once you confirm schemas and redaction behave as expected.

docs.title: Simulator support
docs.text: Sentinel DV is simulator-agnostic. It indexes exported verification artifacts and exposes them through read-only MCP tools; it does not start simulator jobs, open proprietary databases, or stream raw waveform files.

docs.title: Supported artifact types
docs.text: Artifact Files indexed today Notes UVM logs *.log Parses common UVM report lines from VCS, Questa, Xcelium, Verilator, and generic logs. cocotb/JUnit results.xml, results_*.xml, junit.xml, *junit*.xml Produces tests and failure events. Assertions *.assert.json, *.assertions.txt, assertions*.rpt, vcs_assert*.log, vsim_assertions*.log, questa_assertions*.txt Produces assertion definitions and runtime failures. Coverage summaries coverage.json, coverage_summary.json, coverage.xml, *.cov.json, *.cov.txt, coverage.dat.summary, dashboard.html (VCS URG), overalldu.js (Questa vcover) Exported summaries or HTML/JS reports from URG/vcover are all supported. Raw proprietary databases (UCDB, VDB) are not parsed directly. Waveform summaries *.wave.json, *_waveform.json, waveform_summary.json, *.vcd VCD can be parsed directly; FSDB/WLF/SHM/VPD should be converted to bounded JSON summaries first.

docs.title: Checked-in simulator examples
docs.text:
Simulator Fixture Verify all MCP tools VCS demo/vcs_counter/ python scripts/verify_all_mcp_tools.py --sim vcs Questa demo/questa_counter/ python scripts/verify_all_mcp_tools.py --sim questa Cadence Xcelium demo/cadence_counter/ python scripts/verify_all_mcp_tools.py --sim cadence Verilator demo/verilator_counter/ python scripts/verify_all_mcp_tools.py --sim verilator

Run all simulator fixtures:

python examples/simulator_matrix.py --sim all

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Point artifact_roots at directories that contain exported artifacts:

artifact_roots:
  - ./demo/vcs_counter

index:
  type: duckdb
  path: ./sentinel_dv.db

adapters:
  uvm: true
  cocotb: true
  assertions: true
  coverage: true
  waveform_summary: true

Then build the index:

sentinel-dv-index --config config.yaml --index-all

Relative paths in config.yaml are resolved relative to the config file location.

docs.title: VCS
docs.text:
Export text reports and summaries next to your regression artifacts:

vcs -sverilog -full64 -debug_access+all -l simv.log ...
./simv +UVM_TESTNAME=my_test -l run.log

Recommended files for Sentinel DV:

  • results.xml from your regression runner or CI harness
  • run.log or simv.log
  • assertions/*.assert.json or bounded assertion report text
  • coverage/coverage.json or exported XML/text summaries
  • coverage/report/dashboard.html from urg -report — automatically detected and parsed for LINE, TOGGLE, ASSERT, GROUP, and SCORE percentages
  • waveforms/*.wave.json generated from VPD/FSDB/VCD as a bounded summary

docs.title: Questa
docs.text:
Use Questa logs and exported summaries:

vlog counter.sv tb.sv
vsim -c work.tb -do "run -all; quit" -l vsim.log
vcover report -html -output coverage_html coverage.ucdb

Point artifact_roots at the HTML report directory (the one that contains files/overalldu.js):

artifact_roots:
  - path/to/coverage_html/files   # contains overalldu.js — auto-detected and parsed

The files/overalldu.js data file is automatically detected (confirmed by a var g_data block with "ds" key) and parsed for statement, branch, toggle, assertion, functional, and total coverage percentages.

For other coverage/assertion/waveform data, export to bounded JSON/XML/text files before indexing. Raw WLF/UCDB files are not parsed directly.

docs.title: Cadence Xcelium
docs.text:
Use Xcelium logs and exported summaries:

xrun -sv -coverage all counter.sv tb.sv -l xrun.log

HTML coverage reports — Sentinel DV directly parses Xcelium IMC HTML reports generated by:

imc -exec "load coverage.vdb; report -html -out html_report"
# or
xcrg -report -db coverage.vdb -reportdir html_report

Place cov_report.html, imc_summary.html, or xcoverage_report.html in an artifact root and Sentinel DV auto-detects and parses them (the coverage.summary and coverage.trend MCP tools will include Xcelium metrics).

For other coverage/assertion/waveform data, export to bounded JSON/XML/text files before indexing. Raw SHM/ICCR coverage databases are not parsed directly.

docs.title: UVM log parsing details
docs.text:
Sentinel DV ships patterns for the four common UVM log formats:

Format Example line VCS native UVM_ERROR /path/file.svh(10) @ 887915000000: uvm_test_top.comp [TAG] message VCS Jenkins UVM_ERROR /path/file.svh @ 887915000000: uvm_test_top.comp message Questa # UVM_ERROR @ 100 ns: uvm_test_top.comp message Generic fallback UVM_ERROR @ 100 ns: message

Patterns are tried in the order shown; the first match wins.

Count-summary lines are always skipped: VCS appends UVM_ERROR : 0 and Questa appends # UVM_ERROR : 0 at end-of-simulation to report per-severity counts. These lines are not failures and are filtered before any pattern is attempted. Additionally, the report demote/catch counters (Number of caught UVM_FATAL reports : 4, Number of demoted UVM_ERROR reports : 0) are also filtered — these are housekeeping statistics, not individual failure events.

Test status values — the parser returns one of three statuses:

Status Meaning pass No UVM_ERROR/FATAL, simulation completed normally (VCS report, $finish, or UVM TEST DONE present) fail UVM_ERROR or UVM_FATAL messages found, or explicit FAILED marker present aborted No UVM errors, but the simulation never reached a clean exit — typically a license pre-emption, OOM kill, or run-script timeout that terminated the process mid-simulation

The aborted status is important: a simulation that exits abnormally (ending with just Releasing License for VCS-BASE-RUNTIME but no VCS Simulation Report footer) was previously mis-classified as pass. The parser now correctly distinguishes a clean zero-error exit from a mid-flight process kill.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
Sentinel DV keeps simulator support artifact-based by design:

  • MCP tools are read-only.
  • Evidence paths are normalized and cannot escape configured artifact roots.
  • Output size, evidence count, and excerpts are bounded by security settings.
  • Redaction is applied to parsed log messages and failure details.

docs.title: “No configuration found…”
docs.text: Sentinel DV requires a config file. Use either: - Create config first: cp config.example.yaml config.yaml (required — no automatic demo/ fallback) - python -m sentinel_dv.server --config /path/to/config.yaml - or export SENTINEL_DV_CONFIG=/path/to/config.yaml and then run python -m sentinel_dv.server

docs.title: “Index not ready…”
docs.text:
If a tool fails with INDEX_NOT_READY, run indexing first:

python -m sentinel_dv.indexing.indexer --config config.yaml --index-all

docs.title: Tool errors (structured)
docs.text:
Tool responses follow this error shape:

{
  "schema_version": "1.0.0",
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_ARGUMENT",
    "message": "..."
  }
}

Common code values include: - INVALID_ARGUMENT - INDEX_NOT_READY - NOT_FOUND - PERMISSION_DENIED - INTERNAL - LIMIT_EXCEEDED

docs.title: Waveform summaries
docs.text:
Sentinel DV does not stream raw FSDB, VCD, or WLF files to MCP clients. Instead, it indexes bounded waveform summaries so agents can answer questions like “which signals toggled?” without loading multi-gigabyte dumps.

Two input formats are supported:

Format Adapter When to use Precomputed JSON (*.wave.json, waveform_summary.json) WaveformSummaryParser Pipelines that already emit JSON summaries VCD (*.vcd) VcdSummaryParser Verilator and other simulators that write Value Change Dump files

Both are built into the sentinel-dv package (no separate install).

docs.title: Enable indexing
docs.text:
adapters:
  waveform_summary: true

Then rebuild the index:

sentinel-dv-index --config config.yaml --index-all

The indexer scans artifact roots for:

  • *.wave.json, *_waveform.json, waveform_summary.json
  • *.vcd

Summaries are stored in DuckDB and linked to tests by test_name.

docs.title: Linking waveforms to tests
docs.text:
Each waveform file must resolve to an already indexed test:

  1. Exact or suffix match on tests.name (e.g. test_counter_sim matches counter_tb.test_counter_sim).
  2. Optional framework in JSON (for *.wave.json only); VCD lookup falls back without framework if needed.
  3. VCD file naming: use {test_name}.vcd (e.g. test_counter_sim.vcd for JUnit testcase test_counter_sim).

If no test matches, the file is skipped silently during indexing.

docs.title: Precomputed JSON format
docs.text:
Example (demo/waveforms/test_increment.wave.json):

{
  "test_name": "test_counter.test_increment",
  "framework": "cocotb",
  "format": "precomputed-vcd",
  "end_time_ns": 50000,
  "signal_groups": [
    {
      "name": "dut",
      "signals": [
        {"name": "clk", "width": 1, "toggles": 100, "last_value": "1"},
        {"name": "count", "width": 8, "toggles": 8, "last_value": "0x05"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "highlights": [
    {"time_ns": 10000, "signal": "count", "value": "0x01", "note": "first increment"}
  ]
}

Required fields:

  • test_name (string)
  • signals (array) or signal_groups (array of {name, signals})

Optional: framework, format, end_time_ns, highlights, metadata.

docs.title: VCD format (built-in parser)
docs.text:
VcdSummaryParser (sentinel_dv/adapters/vcd_summary.py) reads standard VCD files and computes per-signal:

  • Toggle counts (full trace at index time, or within a window at query time)
  • value_at_start / value_at_end when a window is requested
  • $timescale conversion so # timestamps map to nanoseconds

Hierarchical duplicate signal names in the dump are merged by name.

docs.title: Time windows (20–30 µs example)
docs.text:
MCP tools accept optional start_time_ns and end_time_ns (always nanoseconds):

Human unit Nanoseconds for API 20 µs 20000 30 µs 30000

Example MCP call (after indexing a VCD):

{
  "test_id": "t_…",
  "start_time_ns": 20000,
  "end_time_ns": 30000
}

For indexed VCD files, Sentinel DV re-opens the source .vcd under artifact_roots and parses only that window (values + toggles inside the range). Both parameters are required together.

For JSON summaries, the window filters highlights only; use VCD for per-signal window values.

Summary only

This is not a waveform viewer. Very large VCDs are read sequentially; only aggregated stats are stored.

docs.title: MCP tools
docs.text:
After indexing, query by test_id:

Tool Returns wave.signals Signal list (value_at_start, value_at_end, toggles, …); optional start_time_ns / end_time_ns wave.summary Format, highlights, metadata; optional time window

If no summary exists for a test, tools return NOT_FOUND with guidance to enable waveform_summary and re-index.

docs.title: Releasing Sentinel DV
docs.text: Releases are tag-driven: pushing v* triggers PyPI, GitHub Release, and MCP registry publish. Do not tag until every step below passes — the release workflow runs the same gates, but fixing issues after publish is painful.

docs.title: 1. Land changes on main with green CI
docs.text:
Every push to main runs CI:

  • Ruff + Black
  • Full test suite + ≥70% coverage
  • Wheel import smoke (Python 3.12 job)

Wait for CI to succeed before releasing.

docs.title: 2. Run pre-release locally
docs.text:
./scripts/pre_release.sh vX.Y.Z

This runs the same checks as CI plus version alignment. Example:

# After bumping pyproject.toml to 1.3.2 and updating docs pins:
./scripts/pre_release.sh v1.3.2

Without a tag (version bump only):

./scripts/pre_release.sh

docs.title: 3. Version bump checklist
docs.text:
Update all of these to the same X.Y.Z:

File Field pyproject.toml version = "X.Y.Z" sentinel_dv/__init__.py __version__ server.json top-level and packages[].version README.md title + >=X.Y.Z / @X.Y.Z docs/index.md hero badge docs/getting-started/installation.md current release + pip pin docs/getting-started/quick-start.md pip pin + server banner examples/*.md, mkdocs.yml install pins CHANGELOG.md new [X.Y.Z] section docs/about/changelog.md new section + link

python scripts/check_versions.py vX.Y.Z verifies the critical paths.

docs.text:
• Mandatory config: cp config.example.yaml in installation + quick-start
  • Changelog entry for user-visible changes
  • docs/release/vX.Y.Z-checklist.md (copy from prior checklist)

docs.title: 5. Tag and push (publishes)
docs.text:
git add -A
git commit -m "Release vX.Y.Z: <short summary>"
git push origin main

git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z

The Release workflow will:

  1. Run preflight (lint, tests, coverage, version vs tag)
  2. Build wheel, publish PyPI, GitHub Release, MCP registry

docs.title: v2.0.0 Implementation Brief — Agent Handoff Document
docs.text: Purpose: This document is a complete, self-contained brief for an agent (or developer) taking over implementation of Sentinel DV v2.0.0. Read it fully before writing a single line of code. Every feature below has been scoped against the existing codebase at v1.3.0. File paths, schema conventions, error codes, and naming patterns are already established — follow them exactly so the new work integrates without friction.

docs.title: How to Read This Document
docs.text: Each feature section is structured as: 1. What it is — the user-facing capability 2. Why it belongs in v2.0.0 — the DV engineering motivation 3. Exact implementation plan — files to create or modify, schemas to define, DB tables to add, MCP tools to register, tests to write 4. Invariants to preserve — constraints the existing architecture enforces that must not be broken

docs.title: Codebase Orientation (Read First)
docs.text:
Before implementing anything, understand these entry points:

File Role sentinel_dv/server.py All MCP tool registrations via @mcp.tool(name=...) + @_tool_wrapper sentinel_dv/tools/core.py Tool logic — receives IndexStore, returns dict[str, Any] sentinel_dv/indexing/store.py DuckDB backend — all table DDL, queries, inserts sentinel_dv/indexing/indexer.py Artifact scanner that populates the store sentinel_dv/schemas/ Pydantic models used for validation in tool responses sentinel_dv/adapters/ Per-format parsers (uvm_log, cocotb, coverage, assertions, waveform) sentinel_dv/config.py SentinelDVConfig, SecurityLimits, AdaptersConfig — all new config goes here sentinel_dv/tools/errors.py ToolError with typed ErrorCode literals — always raise this, never raw exceptions sentinel_dv/tools/validate.py list_response, detail_response, item_response, validate_id, clamp_pagination tests/unit/test_mcp_tools.py Unit tests for tool logic tests/integration/ End-to-end tests against real demo fixtures tests/security/test_path_traversal.py Security tests — add path-related tests here

Naming conventions in use: - MCP tool names: noun.verb (e.g., runs.list, coverage.summary, assertions.failures) - DB table names: plural snake_case (e.g., assertion_failures, coverage_summaries) - Schema classes: PascalCase Pydantic BaseModel (e.g., CoverageMetric, FailureEvent) - Error codes: SCREAMING_SNAKE from ErrorCode Literal in tools/errors.py - Config fields: snake_case under the appropriate config sub-model

MCP tool registration pattern (copy this exactly): 

@mcp.tool(name="feature.action")
@_tool_wrapper
def feature_action(
    param: str = Field(..., description="Clear description with example value"),
    optional_param: str | None = Field(None, description="Optional. What it filters."),
    page: int = Field(1, description="Page number (1-based)"),
    page_size: int = Field(100, description="Items per page"),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    One-line summary of what this tool does.

    Returns: description of the response shape.
    Use when: describe the agent scenario that should trigger this tool.
    """
    return core.feature_action(get_store(), param, optional_param=optional_param, page=page, page_size=page_size)

Architecture invariant: The MCP server is strictly read-only for artifact data. The two write-adjacent features below (job submission, replay) are implemented as command generation, not execution. The server never shells out, never writes to artifact roots, never modifies the DuckDB index from an MCP tool call.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A tool runs.submit that accepts a suite name, optional seed override, optional test filter, and optional simulator hint, and returns a ready-to-execute shell command string that the user (or their CI system) can run to kick off a new regression. The server does not execute the command. It generates it from a configurable command template.

docs.title: Why it belongs here
docs.text: A DV engineer's daily loop is: look at yesterday's regression → find failures → fix RTL → re-run the suite. Right now Claude can do steps 1–3 but step 4 requires the engineer to manually construct the LSF/SLURM/makefile command. This closes that loop. The agent can call runs.submit and hand the engineer a copy-pasteable command with the right seed, test filter, and simulator flags already filled in.

docs.title: 1. Config — sentinel_dv/config.py
docs.text:
Add a new sub-model SubmitConfig inside SentinelDVConfig:

class SimulatorTemplate(BaseModel):
    """Command template for a specific simulator."""
    simulator: str = Field(..., description="Simulator name (vcs|questa|xcelium|verilator)")

        description=(
            "Shell command template. Available placeholders: "
            "{suite}, {seed}, {test_filter}, {extra_args}, {artifact_root}"

class SubmitConfig(BaseModel):
    """Regression job submission configuration."""
    enabled: bool = Field(default=False, description="Enable runs.submit tool")
    default_simulator: str = Field(default="vcs", description="Default simulator name")
    templates: list[SimulatorTemplate] = Field(
        default_factory=list,
        description="Per-simulator command templates",
    )
    lsf_queue: str | None = Field(None, description="LSF queue name (wraps command in bsub)")
    slurm_partition: str | None = Field(None, description="SLURM partition (wraps in sbatch)")

Also add max_command_length: int = Field(default=4096, ...) to SecurityLimits.

class SubmitRequest(BaseModel):
    suite: str                        # Required. Suite name from existing runs.
    simulator: str | None             # Optional. Falls back to submit.default_simulator.
    seed: int | None                  # Optional. Integer seed to reproduce a specific test.

    suite: str
    simulator: str
    seed: int | None
    command: str                      # The generated shell command. Bounded by max_command_length.
    scheduler_command: str | None     # If lsf_queue or slurm_partition configured, the wrapped form.

docs.title: 3. Tool logic — sentinel_dv/tools/core.py
docs.text:
Add function generate_submit_command(store, suite, simulator, seed, test_filter, extra_args):

  • Validate suite exists in the store (store.count_runs() filtered by suite > 0 or directly query). If suite unknown, raise ToolError("NOT_FOUND", f"Suite '{suite}' has no indexed runs. Check runs.list for valid suite names.").
  • Look up config get_config().submit. If not config.submit.enabled, raise ToolError("PERMISSION_DENIED", "runs.submit is disabled. Set submit.enabled: true in config.yaml.").
  • Find matching SimulatorTemplate for the requested simulator. If none found, raise ToolError("INVALID_ARGUMENT", f"No template for simulator '{simulator}'. Available: {[t.simulator for t in config.submit.templates]}.").
  • Interpolate the template using str.format_map with a safe mapping that leaves unknown placeholders as literal text (do not use .format() — user-controlled extra_args could contain braces).
  • Wrap in LSF bsub -q {queue} "{command}" or SLURM sbatch --partition={partition} --wrap="{command}" if configured.
  • Truncate to max_command_length and return SubmitResponse.

docs.title: 4. Server registration — sentinel_dv/server.py
docs.text:
@mcp.tool(name="runs.submit")
@_tool_wrapper
def runs_submit(
    suite: str = Field(..., description="Suite name to run (must exist in runs.list)"),
    simulator: str | None = Field(None, description="Simulator override (vcs|questa|xcelium|verilator). Defaults to submit.default_simulator in config."),
    seed: int | None = Field(None, description="Seed to fix for reproducing a specific test. Omit for random."),
    test_filter: str | None = Field(None, description="Test name glob or pattern to run a subset (e.g. 'axi_burst_*')."),
    extra_args: str | None = Field(None, description="Extra simulator arguments appended verbatim to the generated command."),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Generate a ready-to-run regression command for a suite.

    Does NOT execute the command. Returns the shell command string for the user
    to copy-paste or pipe to their CI system.
    Use when: the engineer has reviewed failures and wants to re-run the suite
    with a seed fix, test filter, or simulator override.
    """
    return core.generate_submit_command(
        get_store(), suite=suite, simulator=simulator,
        seed=seed, test_filter=test_filter, extra_args=extra_args,
    )

docs.title: Feature 2: Live Simulator Hook (State Polling Adapter)
What it is
docs.text:
A new adapter (sentinel_dv/adapters/live_sim.py) that reads a well-defined live state file that a running simulator writes periodically (a small JSON sidecar), and a new MCP tool sim.status that returns the current simulation progress without needing to wait for the run to finish and be indexed.

The server does not connect to a simulator process, does not use TCP/IPC, and does not execute any commands. It reads a JSON file from the artifact root that the simulator's UVM test (or a Makefile wrapper) is responsible for writing. This keeps the read-only invariant.

docs.title: Why it belongs here
docs.text: Coverage closure campaigns run for hours. An engineer running a nightly wants to check mid-run: how many tests have finished, what's the current pass rate, are there early fatals that should trigger an abort? Today they must SSH into the compute node. With sim.status Claude can answer this from the indexed live-state file.

docs.title: 1. Live state file format (document + validate)
docs.text:
Create sentinel_dv/schemas/live_sim.py:

class LiveSimProgress(BaseModel):
    """Schema for the live simulation state sidecar file."""
    suite: str
    run_id: str                        # Matches the run_id that will be indexed when done.
    simulator: str
    started_at: str                    # RFC3339
    as_of: str                         # RFC3339 — when this file was last written
    phase: Literal["compiling", "elaborating", "running", "finishing", "done", "aborted"]
    total_tests: int
    completed_tests: int
    passed_tests: int
    failed_tests: int
    active_tests: list[str]            # Names of currently running tests (bounded to 20)
    recent_errors: list[str]           # Last N UVM_ERROR/FATAL lines (bounded to 10, redacted)
    estimated_finish_at: str | None    # RFC3339 or None

Document the file path convention: {artifact_root}/{suite}/live_status.json. The simulator wrapper (Makefile, Python script, or UVM reporting callback) is responsible for writing this file every N seconds. Provide a reference Makefile snippet in docs/guides/live-sim.md.

    def __init__(self, artifact_roots: list[str], redactor: Redactor): ...

        """

        Returns None if no live file found (sim not running or not configured).
        Applies redactor to recent_errors before returning.
        Validates with LiveSimProgress — raises ToolError("INTERNAL", ...) on schema violation.
        """

Set adapters.live_sim: true in config.yaml."). - Instantiate LiveSimAdapter with config artifact roots and default redactor. - Call read_status(suite). If None, raise ToolError("NOT_FOUND", f"No live_status.json found for suite '{suite}'. Is the simulation running with the live-sim adapter enabled?"). - Check as_of age against live_sim_max_age_seconds. If stale, return the data but include "stale": true, "stale_seconds": N in the response so the agent can warn the user. - Return detail_response({**status.model_dump(), "stale": False}).

@mcp.tool(name="sim.status")
@_tool_wrapper
def sim_status(

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
Two new MCP tools — assertions.sva_status and assertions.vacuity — that expose:

  1. assertions.sva_status: for each SVA property indexed, whether it fired (antecedent matched and consequent was checked), passed, failed, never triggered (vacuous), or was disabled during the run. Requires a new sva_runs table.

  2. assertions.vacuity: lists all assertions that were enabled but never had their antecedent triggered across a given run — the "dead assertion" problem. These are assertions that give false confidence because they never actually checked anything.

docs.title: Why it belongs here
docs.text: In any UVM/SVA regression, vacuous assertion passes are a silent quality problem. An assertion like assert property (@clk axi_valid |-> ##[1:4] axi_ready) shows 0 failures but may have never been triggered if the stimulus never drove axi_valid. Today there is no tool to surface this. An agent with assertions.vacuity can proactively flag: "12 AXI protocol assertions never fired in this run — your stimulus may not be exercising the AXI bus."

docs.title: 1. New DB table — sentinel_dv/indexing/store.py
docs.text:
Add to _create_schema():

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sva_run_status (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    test_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    assertion_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'fired_pass' | 'fired_fail' | 'vacuous' | 'disabled' | 'unknown'
    fire_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    pass_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    fail_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    vacuous_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sva_run ON sva_run_status(run_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sva_test ON sva_run_status(test_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sva_assertion ON sva_run_status(assertion_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sva_status ON sva_run_status(status);

Add store methods: 

def insert_sva_status(self, run_id, test_id, assertion_id, status, fire_count, pass_count, fail_count, vacuous_count) -> None: ...
def query_sva_status(self, run_id=None, test_id=None, assertion_id=None, status=None, page=1, page_size=100) -> tuple[list[dict], int]: ...

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
A tool coverage.gaps that analyzes the coverage database for a run and returns: 1. Uncovered bins — coverpoints with covered < 100% and their bins_missed lists. 2. Recommended test patterns — heuristic suggestions for what kind of stimulus would cover each uncovered bin, derived from the bin name, scope, and any assertion tag metadata. 3. Priority ordering — gaps ordered by how many other metrics share the same scope (a scope with 5 uncovered coverpoints is higher priority than one with 1).

This is purely analytical — it reads coverage_summaries and assertions from DuckDB and applies deterministic heuristics. It does not call an LLM internally.

docs.title: Why it belongs here
docs.text: coverage.summary already shows what is covered. The missing step is telling the engineer what to do about it. A DV engineer looking at 87.5% AXI functional coverage wants to know: "which bins are missing, and what test stimulus closes them?" Today that requires manually reading the coverage report and cross-referencing with the testplan. coverage.gaps does this cross-reference automatically from what's already indexed.

docs.title: 3. Tool logic — sentinel_dv/tools/core.py
docs.text:
Add get_coverage_gaps(store, run_id, kind=None, min_covered_pct=None, page=1, page_size=50):

  • validate_id(run_id, "run_id") then verify run exists.
  • Query all coverage_summaries for the run (with optional kind filter).
  • For each summary, iterate metrics. Collect metrics where covered < 100.0 and bins_missed is non-empty.
  • Compute priority per scope: count how many uncovered metrics share the same scope prefix (first two dot-separated components of scope). Scopes with more uncovered metrics get lower priority number (higher priority).
  • Sort gaps by priority ASC, then covered_pct ASC (most uncovered first within same priority).
  • For each gap, call generate_recommendations(metric_name, scope, bins_missed).
  • Apply pagination. Clamp to max_coverage_gaps.
  • Return CoverageGapsResponse.

Optional parameter min_covered_pct: float | None — if set, only return gaps where covered < min_covered_pct. Useful for "show me only metrics below 50% coverage."

docs.title: 4. Server registration — sentinel_dv/server.py
docs.text:
@mcp.tool(name="coverage.gaps")
@_tool_wrapper
def coverage_gaps(
    run_id: str = Field(..., description="Run identifier to analyze coverage gaps for"),
    kind: str | None = Field(None, description="Coverage kind filter: functional|code|assertion|toggle|fsm"),
    min_covered_pct: float | None = Field(None, description="Only return gaps below this coverage percentage (0-100). E.g. 80.0 shows metrics below 80% covered."),
    page: int = Field(1, description="Page number"),
    page_size: int = Field(50, description="Items per page (max 100)"),
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Analyze coverage gaps for a run and suggest closure stimulus.

    Returns uncovered coverpoints ordered by priority (scopes with more gaps first),
    with heuristic recommendations for what stimulus would close each gap.
    Use when: driving coverage closure, identifying what tests or sequences to add next,
    or reporting to a coverage closure review meeting.
    """
    return core.get_coverage_gaps(
        get_store(), run_id=run_id, kind=kind,
        min_covered_pct=min_covered_pct, page=page, page_size=page_size,
    )

docs.title: Output schema
docs.text: Every new tool response must define an outputSchema dict in the @mcp.tool call. Study the FastMCP documentation for the exact syntax. At minimum, document the top-level keys and their types. This is what allows MCP clients to understand responses without calling the tool.

docs.title: Error messages must be actionable
docs.text:
Every ToolError raise must follow this pattern: - Say what went wrong (the factual condition). - Say what to do about it (the corrective action). - Reference the exact config key or tool name to use.

Example: 

# Bad:
raise ToolError("NOT_FOUND", "Suite not found")

# Good:
raise ToolError(
    "NOT_FOUND",
    f"Suite '{suite}' has no indexed runs. "
    f"Check available suites with runs.list, or verify the suite name in your config.yaml artifact_roots."
)

docs.title: Security — command injection prevention
docs.text:
Features 1 and 4 generate shell commands from user-supplied extra_args. Use this pattern:

import shlex

safe_args = shlex.quote(extra_args) if extra_args else ""

Never use subprocess, os.system, or any shell execution. The server must not execute the generated commands under any circumstances.

Suite names and test names used in templates must be validated against a pattern before interpolation:

import re
if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+", suite):
    raise ToolError("INVALID_ARGUMENT", f"Suite name contains invalid characters: '{suite}'")

docs.text:
These were identified in the v1.3.0 review and must be fixed in this release:

Fix 1 — Race condition in sequential ID generation (store.py): The pattern SELECT COALESCE(MAX(id), 0) + 1 FROM assertion_failures is used in multiple insert_* methods. Replace with DuckDB SEQUENCE:

CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS seq_assertion_failure_id START 1;
CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS seq_evidence_id START 1;
CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS seq_coverage_id START 1;
CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS seq_sva_status_id START 1;  -- for new table

Then use nextval('seq_assertion_failure_id') in INSERT statements. Run a migration in _create_schema() using CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS so existing DBs are not broken.

Fix 2 — resolve_config demo fallback must warn loudly:

    return SentinelDVConfig(artifact_roots=[str(demo_root)], ...)

# Fixed (warn on stderr, document the fallback):
